solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Start of rough sketch about decoration for furniture

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word for sketch is read backwards

parts.note: to draw is to sketch

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the OBE (Order of the British Empire) is a British honour

explanation.surface: An artist's rough sketch is planned as decoration on a piece of furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start of rough' looks like it opens the answer, but the reversed sketch comes first: 'about' turns DRAW into WARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A wardrobe is a tall cupboard for hanging clothes, a standard item of bedroom furniture.

clue.text: Young creature putting weight on robust part of leg

parts.note: hale means healthy and robust, as in hale and hearty
the calf is the back of the lower leg

explanation.surface: Someone bulking up the muscle on their lower leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Young creature' is a vague definition that 'calf' in the wordplay helps pin down: a calf is also a young whale.
explanation.definitionFit: A whale calf is the offspring of a whale, so it is a young animal.

clue.text: Consideration about pressure within group

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters

indicators.note: within means the pressure letter sits inside the word for group

parts.note: a sect is a group with shared beliefs
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Thoughtfulness shown about the pressure inside a group.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing respect for someone means giving their feelings or wishes due regard and thought.

clue.text: System heroic monarch set up

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the letters are read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: epic means heroic, grand in scale
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A political system put in place by a heroic king or queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' reverses EPICER, the heroic word plus the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A recipe can mean any method or formula for achieving something, as in a recipe for success.

clue.text: Brute has died for king of island

indicators.note: has died for king means the letter for died takes the place of the letter for king

parts.note: a barbarian is a brute, a savage
R is short for rex, Latin for king
D is the abbreviation for died in genealogies

explanation.surface: A brutal man has died in place of a king, as in an island coup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' tells you D (died) replaces R (king) in BARBARIAN. The island is Barbados.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbadian is the adjective for Barbados, the Caribbean island, so it means belonging to that island.

clue.text: Garment blonde regularly paired with diamonds

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word blonde

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A dress worn by a blonde woman always set off with diamonds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' picks the first, third and fifth letters of 'blonde'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodice is the close-fitting upper part of a woman's dress, an item of clothing.

clue.text: Bread virtually firm after while at home

indicators.note: after puts the firm abbreviation after the word for while

parts.note: a bit means a while, a short time, as in wait a bit
Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: A baker's loaf almost firm after a spell in the oven at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'virtually' looks like a cue to cut a word short, but it belongs to the definition: bread (slang for money) in virtual form.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread is slang for money, and bitcoin is a digital currency, money that exists only online.

clue.text: Parties around start of lockdown journalist revealed

indicators.note: around means the parties word goes round the next letter

parts.note: discos are dance parties

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter exposes parties held in breach of lockdown rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts L, the start of 'lockdown', inside DISCOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Disclosed means made known or brought to light, so it matches revealed as a past tense verb.

clue.text: Sheath covering heel for shower

indicators.note: covering means the sheath word wraps round the word for heel

parts.note: a case is a sheath or protective cover
a heel and a cad are both dishonourable men

explanation.surface: A protective cover over the heel of a shoe, kept on in the shower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heel' is not part of a shoe here: it means a rotter, CAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A cascade is a falling stream, and a shower is a fall of water or things, as in a shower of sparks.

clue.text: Goon Show's, without question, first- class — bring it back

indicators.note: bring it back means the letters built so far are read backwards
without means the question word is removed from the letters of Show's

parts.note: the letters of Show's, ignoring the apostrophe
how is a question word
A means first-class, as in A1 or grade A

explanation.surface: Praise for The Goon Show, the classic BBC radio comedy, as unquestionably first-class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes HOW out of SHOWS to leave SS; add A and 'bring it back' reverses SSA. 'Goon' looks like part of the radio show's name but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A goon is a foolish or stupid person, so it is a synonym for a fool or donkey.

clue.text: Inter scouts strangely ignoring United players

indicators.note: strangely means the remaining letters are put into a new order
ignoring means the letter for United is left out of the fodder

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for United, as in football club names

explanation.surface: Talent spotters from Inter Milan oddly pass over Manchester United's footballers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring' drops U from INTERSCOUTS; 'strangely' rearranges the rest. The surface says football, but the players are musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Cornetists play the cornet, a brass instrument, so they are musical players.

clue.text: Model not totally immune meeting the French Romeo

indicators.note: not totally means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: exempt means free from an obligation, immune
la is French for the (feminine)
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A fashion model who is not quite immune to the charms of a French Romeo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not totally' cuts the T off EXEMPT.
explanation.definitionFit: An exemplar is a perfect example to be copied, which is one sense of a model.

clue.text: One boasts well to film fan having taken out lead characters

indicators.note: lead characters are the first letters of each word, and these are removed from to film fan

explanation.surface: A braggart speaks to a film fan about the leading characters cut from a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having taken out lead characters' strips the first letters from 'to', 'film' and 'fan'. 'boasts' does not mean brags: it means possesses, as a place boasts a view.
explanation.definitionFit: An oilman owns or runs oil wells, so he is someone who has a well.

clue.text: Non-mainstream music by old singer

parts.note: alt is short for alternative, as in alt-rock

explanation.surface: An old-school singer who performs indie music.
explanation.definitionFit: An alto is a vocalist whose range is the lowest female or highest male voice.

clue.text: Spend trips bringing in work

definitions.note: a noun here, money spent, matching the plural noun

indicators.note: bringing in means the word for work goes inside the word for trips

parts.note: outings are trips or excursions
to go is to work or function, as in the engine won't go

explanation.surface: Excursions that include work outings are expensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spend' looks like a verb, but it is the noun, as in a company's annual spend.
explanation.definitionFit: Outgoings are money paid out, the same as a business's spend or expenditure.

clue.text: I'd rejected car part that's degraded

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the letters of I'd are read backwards

parts.note: the letters of I'd, ignoring the apostrophe
the Mini is a classic British small car
to shed is to part with, cast off

explanation.surface: Someone throws out a worn-out bit of their car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' is the reversal signal. 'part' is a verb meaning part with, not a component of the car.
explanation.definitionFit: Diminished means lessened or reduced in standing, close to degraded.

clue.text: Found mobile under cot — one should be above that

indicators.note: in a down answer, the letter placed above the rest comes first

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: mobile means moving, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A baby's mobile turned up under the cot, though it should hang above it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mobile' rearranges UNDERCOT, and 'should be above that' puts I on top of it in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: To found something is to establish or institute it, and introduce can mean bring into use for the first time.

clue.text: Record race including good performance

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record

indicators.note: including means the race word takes in the letter for good

parts.note: to hare is to race along

explanation.surface: A record-breaking race that includes a good performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performance' is the doing of a duty, not a show.
explanation.definitionFit: The discharge of one's duties means carrying them out, their performance.

clue.text: Father worried by idiot accepted by Railway Society

indicators.note: by means set beside, so the letters follow on

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
ate means worried, as in what's eating you

indicators.note: accepted by means the idiot word is taken inside the railway abbreviation

parts.note: a nit is an idiot

explanation.surface: A dad troubled by a fool who has been let into a railway enthusiasts' club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' is not an anagram signal here: ate means worried, as in what's eating you.
explanation.definitionFit: A fraternity is a brotherhood or club of people with shared interests, a society.

clue.text: Account by deceptive figure about right coach for Venus Williams

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the account and liar letters together are read backwards
by means set beside, so the letters follow on

parts.note: a liar is a deceptive person

explanation.surface: A tale about a lying tennis coach working for Venus Williams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses ACLIAR to RAILCA. Venus Williams is American, and railcar is the American word for a railway carriage, which British English calls a coach.
explanation.definitionFit: Railcar is the US word for a railway carriage, so it is what an American calls a coach.

clue.text: Relations having time for papa making quips

indicators.note: having time for papa means the letter for time replaces the letter for papa

parts.note: a relation is an account or report of events
Papa is P in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Family members swapping time with dad for wisecracks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relations' suggests family, but here it means accounts.
explanation.definitionFit: Retorts are sharp or witty replies, which is what quips are.

clue.text: Plant pruned in raised surface

indicators.note: pruned means cut back, so the plant name loses its final letter

parts.note: the daisy is a common flowering plant

explanation.surface: A plant trimmed back in a raised flower bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A dais is a raised platform, as for a speaker in a hall.

clue.text: Freeman maybe split by request from extreme state

indicators.note: split by means the name is broken open and the request word is put inside

parts.note: Alan Freeman was a well-known British radio DJ; maybe marks him as one example of the name
to ask is to request

explanation.surface: A freeman's request causes a split in a state at the far edge of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: Alan 'Fluff' Freeman was a long-running BBC radio DJ. Alaska is the largest, northernmost US state, the extreme one.
explanation.definitionFit: Alaskan describes something from Alaska, the US state at the far north-west extreme of the country.

clue.text: Mounts support on top of deck in ship

indicators.note: in means the support and deck letters go inside the ship abbreviation

parts.note: SS stands for steamship

indicators.note: in a down light, on puts the support above the letter that follows

parts.note: a tee supports a golf ball

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Supports fixed on the upper deck of a ship to hold mounted equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mounts' looks like a verb or fittings; it means horses. 'top of' gives D from 'deck'.
explanation.definitionFit: Steeds are horses for riding, and a mount is a horse one rides.

clue.text: Attack popular song no longer fashionable

parts.note: a hit is a popular song
out means unfashionable, as in in and out of style

explanation.surface: Criticising a chart song that has gone out of fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit out is to attack someone, physically or with harsh words.

clue.text: Turned bath tap too feebly, only part way

indicators.note: Turned says the hidden letters are read backwards
only part signals that just a section of these words is used

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone turned the bath tap so weakly it only opened partway.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'only part way' as the definition, but 'only part' signals the hidden word, leaving 'way' as the definition. 'Turned' reverses the hidden letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A footpath is a path for walkers, a type of way or route.

clue.text: Finger cut badly by opening of early spinning machine

indicators.note: badly means the letters are mangled into a new order
the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A finger badly cut by an early spinning machine, like an old mill accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges FINGERCUT, and 'opening of' takes E from 'early'.
explanation.definitionFit: A centrifuge rotates at high speed to separate substances, so it is a rotating device.

clue.text: Party leader familiarly picked up alcohol

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word sounds like the one named

parts.note: Keir Starmer, Labour Party leader, called by his first name

explanation.surface: The party leader, known by first name, was caught drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: Keir Starmer is the leader of Britain's Labour Party and Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Kir is an aperitif of white wine with blackcurrant liqueur, an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Credit is doubled in emergency

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

indicators.note: doubled means the word is written twice

explanation.surface: A credit crunch doubles into a full-blown emergency.
explanation.definitionFit: A crisis is a time of acute danger or difficulty, an emergency.

clue.text: Images for every relative, each backed

parts.note: per means for each, as in per person
a son is a family relative

indicators.note: backed means reversed, so the abbreviation for each is read backwards

explanation.surface: Photos for every member of the family, each one with a backing.
explanation.definitionFit: Personae are the public images or characters people present to others.
